sections.label: MAS grant to PRGT
sections.summary: Amendments to the Bretton Woods Agreements Act let MAS join the PRGT with a US$20 million grant from Singapore's IMF gold sales profit share.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Bretton Woods Agreements Act will allow MAS to participate in the PRGT through a US$20 million grant paid from Singapore's share of the IMF's gold sales profit.

sections.label: Parliament approval for MAS grant
sections.summary: The Bill requires Parliament's approval by specific resolution for a grant given by MAS to the IMF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Page: 52 Third, specifically in the case of a grant to be given by MAS to the IMF, the Bill provides that Parliament's approval by specific resolution is required.

sections.label: Safeguards for IMF financial assistance
sections.summary: The Bill adds a safeguard requiring early repayment provisions if an IMF programme is suspended or terminated, and lets MAS grant assistance to the PRGT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce a new safeguard for loans and other financial assistance provided to the IMF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Such agreements must include provisions for MAS to require early repayment in the event of suspension, or premature termination, of the IMF programme for which the assistance was provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In particular, the proposed amendments to the Act will allow MAS to make grants and other financial assistances to IMF's concessional lending facility known as Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT).

sections.label: Singapore's PRGT contribution share
sections.summary: Member states agreed to the arrangement and Singapore's share of contribution to the PRGT was US$20 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The member states Page: 53 have agreed to this arrangement and Singapore's share of contribution to PRGT amounted to US$20 million.

sections.label: Other government assistance condition
sections.summary: Section 6A(2)(b) requires MAS to be satisfied at least one other government would provide financial assistance in response to the IMF's request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, section 6A(2)(b) of the Bill states that MAS needs to be satisfied that at least one other government would be willing to provide the financial assistance in response to IMF's request before the grant or financial assistance can be given.

sections.label: Support for amendment Bill safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendment Bill, especially section 6(a)'s safeguards, such as assistance only if another government has provided or intends assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Page: 54 I am supportive of the amendment Bill, in particular, the new addition in section 6(a) with strong safeguards set out when providing the financial assistance, including loans and grants, to the IMF, for example, the arrangement that financial assistance will be given only if at least one other government has provided or intends to provide assistance in response to a similar request from the IMF.

sections.label: Limit for total financial assistance
sections.summary: Asks whether a limit should be set for total financial assistance under section 6A(2)(c)(ii), suggesting approaches such as 1% of GDP, 2% of reserves, or per capita per citizen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, whether we should set a limit for the total financial assistance, including loans, grants and other forms of financial assistance, under section 6A, subsection (2)(c)(ii).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One approach could be via 1% of GDP or about $4 billion, or 2% of reserves or around $5 billion, or on a per capita basis per Singapore citizen.

sections.label: Fiscal policy early warning
sections.summary: Asks what can strengthen fiscal policy for early warning, and whether Gazette publication of key information on IMF loans or grants suffices given few read the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What can we do to further strengthen our fiscal policy to ensure that we can get an early warning in place and steer away from the storm?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the amendment Bill covers public accountability and transparency when we are making any loans or grants to the IMF.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government will publish the key information in the Gazette and, if I could ask, would this suffice, especially as not many people would read the Gazette?

sections.label: MAS committee on loans
sections.summary: Asks whether a special committee in MAS will decide whether Singapore offers the loans or grants.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Is there a special committee in MAS that will be making the decision on whether or not Singapore is to offer the loans or grants?

sections.label: Bretton Woods Amendment Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Bretton Woods Agreements (Amendment) Bill proposes amendments to let MAS lend, give grants, or provide other financial assistance to the IMF for its programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bretton Woods Agreements (Amendment) Bill proposes amendments to the Act to allow MAS to lend or give grants or to provide other financial assistance to the IMF to support its programmes.

sections.label: Loans paid from MAS reserves
sections.summary: The Explanatory Statement states that any loan or grant to the IMF will be paid out of MAS' reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the Explanatory Statement to the Bill states that any loan or grant to the IMF will be paid out of MAS' reserves.

sections.label: President informed of MAS transactions
sections.summary: Article 22B(6) and (7) require MAS and its CEO to inform the President of proposed transactions likely to draw on MAS' reserves, and the President may disapprove.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Article 22B(6) and (7) of the Constitution requires the MAS and its CEO to inform the President of any proposed transaction of the MAS which is likely to draw on MAS' reserves and, the President, acting in his discretion, may disapprove the proposed transaction.

sections.label: MAS grants to IMF trust
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS powers to make grants so Singapore can contribute US$20 million to the IMF's PRGT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: While I appreciate the need to maintain some flexibility as to the form of financial assistance to be provided, given that we have safeguards in the Constitution and the proposed Bill that would engage either or both the President and Parliament, would it not be better for the Bill to specify the types of financial assistance that may be given?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, we must also balance providing financial assistance with exercising prudence when spending our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will provide MAS with additional powers to make grants, in order to enable MAS to participate in the IMF's initiative to strengthen the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT) resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For a start, as the Minister mentioned, Singapore will be able to contribute our share of the IMF's gold sales profit, which will amount to a grant of US$20 million to the PRGT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This proposal for the contribution of the above sales profit is supported by 80% of IMF members and this is a timely move for Singapore to support this as well, in direct response to repeated calls by the IMF for the world to act together, urgently.

sections.label: PRGT lending capacity increase
sections.summary: IMF member pledges raised the PRGT's annual lending capacity from US$1 billion to US$1.75 billion, enough for two decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The pledges made by IMF members so far have increased the PRGT's annual lending capacity from US$1 billion to US$1.75 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The IMF estimates that these additional resources will be able to sustain the PRGT lending for two decades.

sections.label: IMF preferred creditor status
sections.summary: The IMF's preferred creditor status means its loans must be repaid ahead of all other creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As the IMF enjoys preferred creditor status, loans granted by the IMF must be repaid ahead of all other creditors.

sections.label: Singapore quota and IMF repayment
sections.summary: Singapore's quota share is about 0.82%, and under MAS' agreement the IMF must repay loans immediately on request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Singapore's current quota share is about 0.82% of total IMF quotas and this remains a useful benchmark for deriving the financial assistance we provide to the IMF on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under MAS' existing agreement with the IMF, the IMF is obliged to immediately and fully repay the loan upon request.

sections.label: IMF buffer for early repayment
sections.summary: The IMF has set aside more than US$120 billion as a buffer to repay creditors early in an emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The IMF has set aside more than US$120 billion, as a buffer, to ensure its ability to repay creditors early, if and when such an emergency emerges.
